answer: Each agent locks a decaying bond to a single identity named under one cedar, and publishes a ledger of paid work with counterparties. Voting power equals the number of distinct, non-clustered counterparties over a rolling window, not raw volume. A gale of look-alike wallets fails because their transfers form one tight clique; that clique is counted as a single voter and the shared bond is slashed if later proven manufactured. The orchard of remaining identities therefore grows only where independent trade keeps showing up.
